name: Example: Differentiating a Radical Expression
problem:
Consider the function $y = \sqrt[3]{\dfrac{x^2}{x^5+ 1}}.$  The derivative of this function is given by

$$
y' =  \dfrac{g(x)}{3\sqrt[3]{x(x^5+1)^4}}.
$$

Find the function $g(x).$
worked_solution:
Our function can be written as

$$
\begin{aligned}y & =\sqrt[3]{\frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{5}+1}} \\  & =\frac{\sqrt[3]{{x}^{2}}}{\sqrt[3]{{x}^{5}+1}} \\  & =\frac{{x}^{2/3}}{({x}^{5}+1)^{1/3}}.\end{aligned}
$$

First, we take the natural logarithm of both sides and use the quotient and power rules for logarithms:

$$
\begin{aligned}\operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡(\frac{{x}^{2/3}}{({x}^{5}+1)^{1/3}}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{2/3})-\operatorname{ln}⁡(({x}^{5}+1)^{1/3}) \\ \operatorname{ln}⁡y & =\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{5}+1)\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we differentiate both sides with respect to $x{:}$ 

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\operatorname{ln}⁡y) & =\frac{\text{d}}{\text{d}x}(\frac{2}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡x-\frac{1}{3}\operatorname{ln}⁡({x}^{5}+1)) \\ \frac{1}{y}\cdot {y}^{′} & =\frac{2}{3}\cdot \frac{1}{x}-\frac{1}{3}\cdot \frac{1}{{x}^{5}+1}\cdot (5{x}^{4}) \\ \frac{{y}^{′}}{y} & =\frac{1}{3}(\frac{2}{x}-\frac{5{x}^{4}}{{x}^{5}+1})\end{aligned}
$$

 

Now, we solve for $y'{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =y(\frac{1}{3}(\frac{2}{x}-\frac{5{x}^{4}}{{x}^{5}+1}))\end{aligned}
$$

Finally, we substitute $y =  \sqrt[3]{\dfrac{x^2}{x^5+ 1}}{:}$

$$
\begin{aligned}{y}^{′} & =\frac{1}{3}\sqrt[3]{\frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{5}+1}}(\frac{2}{x}-\frac{5{x}^{4}}{{x}^{5}+1}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\sqrt[3]{\frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{5}+1}}(\frac{2({x}^{5}+1)-5{x}^{5}}{x({x}^{5}+1)}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\sqrt[3]{\frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{5}+1}}(\frac{-3{x}^{5}+2}{x({x}^{5}+1)}) \\  & =\frac{1}{3}\sqrt[3]{\frac{{x}^{2}}{{x}^{5}+1}}(\frac{-3{x}^{5}+2}{\sqrt[3]{{x}^{3}({x}^{5}+1)^{3}}}) \\  & =\frac{-3{x}^{5}+2}{3\sqrt[3]{x({x}^{5}+1)^{4}}}\end{aligned}
$$

 

Therefore,

$$
g(x) = \bbox[2pt,Gainsboro]{-3x^5+2}.
$$
